newsitem.title: USA: Reynolds staying in primary aluminum.
newsitem.headline: Reynolds staying in primary aluminum.

text.p: Reynolds Metals Co has decided to stay in the primary aluminum business, chief executive officer Jeremiah Sheehan said Wednesday.

Briefing metals industry analysts on the status of the company's portfolio review, he said Reynolds has also "decided to keep and grow our distribution, specialty building products, and aluminum wheels businesses."
He said the company has exited the U.S. residential construction products business and is exiting the general line extrusion business.
"We have completed the sale of two U.S. extrusion plants, and we plan to sell our extrusion operations in Canada and Spain.

"With respect to our rolling operations, we have announced the sale of our Alabama can stock complex to Alcoa. We are in discussions with several potential buyers regarding the sale of our McCook, Ill., sheet and plate plant. We are pursuing a number of alternatives for our European rolling operations."
He also noted recently announced plans to form a 50-50 joint venture with Quebec's SGF to operate and expand Reynolds' rolling mill in the province.
The company has also sold a reclamation plant in Virginia and its coal properties in Kentucky, and is in the process of selling its aluminum powder and paste plant in Louisville.

Sheehan said the businesses Reynolds has already divested collectively accounted for some $1.9 billion of its 1996 revenues and a net operating investment of $1.2 billion. He said these businesses and those that will be sold or restructured had 1996 operating results that were "about break even."
